title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 5th District
area: Northwestern North Carolina, including Boone, Wilkesboro and the northern foothills.

context.text: Chuck Hubbard won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary. Incumbent Virginia Foxx (R) won her Republican primary. Independent David Clayton did not make the general-election ballot. Robert Luffman advanced from a canceled Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Virginia Foxx

summary.text: Virginia Foxx is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. A longtime member of Congress, she chairs the House Committee on Rules and previously chaired the Committee on Education and the Workforce.

background.text: Born in New York, New York, in 1943; earned a bachelor's degree and M.A.C.T. from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1968, 1972) and an Ed.D. from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (1985).

Worked as an instructor at Caldwell Community College and as an instructor and assistant dean at Appalachian State University; owned a landscape nursery and served as Deputy Secretary for Management at the North Carolina Department of Administration.
Served on the Watauga County Board of Education before her election to Congress.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Rules and also serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Government Operations Subcommittee) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce.
Chaired the House Committee on Education and the Workforce during the 118th Congress (2023-2025).

candidates.researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately. No specific 2026 campaign priorities were located within the research budget beyond her committee leadership record.

candidates.name: Chuck Hubbard
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Kyah Creekmore.

summary.text: Chuck Hubbard is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. He is a journalist campaigning on affordability, public education, and protecting Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security.

background.text: Born in Bryson City, North Carolina; earned a bachelor's degree from Wofford College in 1985.
Career experience includes working as a journalist; has been affiliated with the Wilkes Recovery Revolution, the Wilkes Child Abuse Prevention Team, and the Wilkes Prison Ministry.

priorities.text: Addressing the rising cost of healthcare, housing, child care, groceries and utilities, and raising the minimum wage.
Supporting public education, teachers, and school infrastructure.
Protecting Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security benefits, and access to reproductive healthcare.

positions.summary: Says Congress must raise the minimum wage and shift more of the tax base to wealthy people and corporations to help working families get by.
Pledges to always vote to protect Medicare and Medicaid benefits that North Carolinians depend on.
Says he will always protect a woman's right to choose and access to critical reproductive healthcare.

candidates.researchNotes: Hubbard has not previously held elected office; positions are drawn from his campaign website's platform statement as quoted by Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Robert Luffman
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Robert Luffman is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. He works in transportation and is campaigning against what he calls the two-party system, favoring congressional term limits.

background.text: Career experience includes working in transportation.

priorities.text: Congressional term limits, saying he would only seek to serve up to five total terms himself.
Immigration reform, saying Congress has not meaningfully updated immigration law since 1996.
Marijuana legalization and record expungement for past marijuana charges.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Luffman's 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website was located.
